#17 — DukeSim NAEOTOM Alpha parameters (McCabe)

Letter: F (F_render) · Priority: ★★ · Kind: classical · Papers: F04 · State: see status.json

Dossier for one reverse-engineering target. Update it in the same change as the target's state in status.json. Equations: Unicode inline or fenced text blocks (no MathJax; the site is offline).

Concept

McCabe, Harrawood, Samei & Abadi, Med. Phys. 52(6) 2025 [F04] extend DukeSim with a photon-counting detector model for the Siemens NAEOTOM Alpha. The model has three parts:

  • per-threshold quantum efficiency;
  • 3 × 3 crosstalk;
  • a spatio-energetic noise covariance between thresholds.

They validate it against the real scanner on the ACR and Mercury phantoms. DukeSim and the detector response files are not public. The value F can take is the published acquisition and detector parameters. Written as an XCIST configuration, they give a Siemens photon-counting hook without the closed simulator. Nothing was decompiled. Full text was read from PMC12285274, because it is not in papers/.

Equations

S_t(x, y) = Σ_E  N(E) · QE_t(E) · Σ_{3×3} X_t(E; i, j) · exp(−∫µ(E) dl)      ([F04] eq. 1, threshold t)
noise     = correlated Gaussian with the spatio-energetic covariance (Cholesky)  ([F04] §2.2)
f50       = frequency where MTF = 0.5, measured on an air edge                   ([F04] §2.9)

XCIST's Detection_PC provides threshold binning with a CZT response. It does not provide F04's CdTe crosstalk/covariance model.

Parameters

Parameter Value Source
tube 120 kV [F04 §2.9]
thresholds 20, 65 keV [F04 §2.9]
detector pixel 0.4 mm at isocentre [F04 §2.2]
collimation / pitch 144 × 0.4 mm / 0.8 [F04 §2.9]
rotation 0.5 s [F04 §2.9]
dose levels 1.5 / 3 / 6 / 12 mGy = 19 / 38 / 72 / 152 mAs [F04 §2.9]
recon ReconCT, QIR-3, Br40/Br56/Br64, 0.4 mm [F04 §2.9]
SID / SDD 595 / 1085.6 mm assumed (F04 lists them as inputs, not values)
sensor CdTe [F04 §2.2]; XCIST ships only a CZT 0.25 mm response, so it is approximated

Config: ../xcist/naeotom_alpha.cfg (cited per line; "(assumed)" / "(reduced)" marked).

Paper's claimed result

[F04] Table 1 gives MTF f50 for the real scanner in the ACR phantom:

  • 0.39 ± 0.003 mm⁻¹ (Br40);
  • 0.77 (Br56);
  • 1.08 (Br64).

DukeSim gives 0.39 / 0.73 / 0.97. Noise magnitude tracks dose with errors of 0.07–1.59 HU on 70 keV VMI (§3.1.1).

Our reproduction (number + figure)

Command: python -m F_render.repro.r17_naeotom_spectrum. Run dir: F_render/runs/*-repro-17/ (four photon-counting XCIST scans of a Ø 200 mm water cylinder, ~25 min CPU).

Quantity Ours (simulated, XCIST) Paper [F04]
f50, pre-registered kernel 'standard' 0.573 mm⁻¹ (+47 %) 0.39 mm⁻¹ (real, Br40)
f50, kernel 'soft' (checked afterwards, informational) 0.463 mm⁻¹ (+19 %) 0.39 mm⁻¹
noise vs dose, 19 → 152 mAs 65.0 / 46.2 / 33.3 / 23.0 HU, σ ∝ mAs^−0.501 tracks dose (Fig. 3)
water HU 12.6 → 12.0 HU 0 ± 2 HU after water calibration
  • Agreement on f50: disagree. The pre-registered XCIST 'standard' FBP kernel is sharper than Br40 + QIR. It lies between the paper's Br40 (0.39) and Br56 (0.77).
    • The informational 'soft' kernel lands within 25 %, but it was chosen after seeing the result, so it is not claimed.
  • Noise: the noise–dose exponent is the quantum-limited −0.5 that a correct photon-counting model must show.
  • Not reproduced:
    • F04's real-vs-simulated noise errors (needs the real scanner);
    • QIR;
    • the 70 keV VMI.

Figure: r17-naeotom.png.

Adaptation

  • What the cfg is: an XCIST photon-counting configuration with F04's parameters (T1 ≥ 20 keV summed image), not a DukeSim clone.
  • Missing pieces: the CdTe response, crosstalk and inter-threshold covariance are missing. XCIST's FBP 'standard' kernel stands in for Br40 + QIR-3.
  • Valid uses: a Siemens-flavoured photon-counting forward model for #16-style insertions and for H's noise/MTF sensitivity studies.
  • Not valid: a stand-in for the real scanner.

Verdict

dissected (config delivered, published number not matched). The configuration is usable as a labelled approximation: it has the right geometry class, pixel, thresholds, kV and dose levels, and quantum-limited noise. The resolution does not match Br40 without kernel tuning, which we do not claim.

What to reuse next

  • H: sweep the four F04 dose levels to test whether detector-level noise realism changes the validation metrics.
  • INT / Siemens: if Siemens or Duke can provide the PCCT response (QE, crosstalk, covariance), drop it into XCIST's Detection_PC response slot.
